headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Users
short_summary: This bill directs Dominion Energy Virginia to propose allocating certain grid infrastructure costs to large energy users (25 MW or greater), aiming to reduce the burden on residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Governor Abigail Spanberger, residential ratepayers, consumer advocates.
opponents: Large energy users, data center industry.
news_headline: SCC Requires Data Centers to Pay for New Transmission Infrastructure
news_summary: The State Corporation Commission (SCC) ordered data centers to cover the cost of transmission infrastructure built exclusively for them, saving Virginia families and small businesses hundreds of millions of dollars. This decision followed Governor Spanberger's urging to protect Virginians from shouldering new energy costs.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This legislation requires water suppliers to report the total volume of water, including reclaimed water, provided to data centers, enhancing transparency and informing water resource management.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservation advocates, Virginia League of Conservation Voters, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Data center industry (potentially due to increased reporting burden).
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new state law, championed by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage, with the numbers to be made publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to provide credible data for informed discourse, especially given concerns about data center water consumption during droughts.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Studies
short_summary: This law requires local governments to review potential impacts, including noise studies for homes and schools within 500 feet, before approving new data centers using 100 megawatts or more of electricity.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, Del. Joshua E. Thomas, Del. Sam Rasoul.
opponents: Data center industry, developers (potentially due to increased regulatory burden and restrictions).
news_headline: A Roanoke Delegate Helped Write Virginia's New Data Center Law
news_summary: This new law, which took effect July 1, 2026, requires developers of large data centers (100 MW or more) to conduct noise studies and utilities to disclose substation information, though it does not set specific limits. It aims to give local governments more tools for informed decision-making regarding data center development.
